subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should OpenClaw default unset sandbox Docker `pidsLimit` to 1024 for existing and new users, and what opt-out or migration documentation must accompany that change?
rationale: The patch improves host DoS resistance but changes the default container resource boundary for existing deployments, so automation should not choose the limit or rollout contract by itself.

options.title: Approve default 1024 with opt-out proof
options.body: Merge after adding docs/tests and real Docker proof that unset uses 1024 while explicit overrides, including any unlimited opt-out, are preserved.

options.title: Preserve current unset behavior
options.body: Keep Docker's current unset behavior for existing users and document operator-configured `pidsLimit` as the hardening path.

options.title: Decide resource limits together
options.body: Pause this one-field change until PID, CPU, and memory defaults are handled by a maintainer-owned sandbox resource-limit policy.

recommendation.title: Approve default 1024 with opt-out proof
recommendation.body: Merge after adding docs/tests and real Docker proof that unset uses 1024 while explicit overrides, including any unlimited opt-out, are preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS assigns the sandbox security surface to this group, and the unresolved question is a sandbox boundary default.
